preamble: Click loss in East Kalahari Khoe (Shua and Tshwa clusters: Cara, ǀXaise, Danisi, Deti, Kua, Tsua). Here the palatal click series of Proto-Kalahari Khoe has been largely replaced, mostly by non-click palatal consonants (Tsua and southern Kua still keep some palatal clicks), a regular sound change documented by Traill & Vossen (1997). Sands & Gunnink (2019) note that Khoe click loss increases with distance from the Kalahari core and may be sped up by contact with languages that lack clicks. Western languages such as ǀGwi and Kxoe, and Ts'ixa, which often has the click (partly through contact with Kxoe), keep it, e.g. ǀGwi ǂéē (Nakagawa 2006), Ts'ixa ǂé 'ear'. In the word *ɳǂũ 'sit', with a nasal vowel, the nasal palatal click became the palatal nasal [ɲ] in all seven East Kalahari varieties, including Ts'ixa. This is not the general outcome of *ɳǂ: in *ɳǂu 'black' it gives nʓ, ʓ, d or y (the GLD reconstructs Proto-East Kalahari *ɳǂ- > *nʓ- as regular), so the nasal vowel may condition ɲ. Only one etymon is available in the GLD 110-item list, so certainty is 2, although it is attested in seven varieties. Forms follow the GLD's transcription (Vossen 1997 data). In that system ɕ and ʓ are palatal (alveolo-palatal) affricates [tɕ, dʑ], y is [j], and ʸ marks palatalization.
